# retain the lone-tab lifecycle oracle while old terminals are still served

Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513

## TLDR
This intermediate commit still serves old tmux terminals, but deletes the tests proving that a surviving shell tab is found and protected after the agent's window/terminal has disappeared. General host-tab tests exercise the consent rule without the legacy discovery boundary that originally hid such tabs. No actual destructive regression is established; the issue is removing that meaningful regression oracle while the behavior is still required.

## Details
Assigned patch lines 1–97 deletes the_delete_guard_sees_a_lone_tab_after_the_agent_window_is_gone, and lines around 182–247 delete stop_closes_a_lone_tmux_tab_without_an_agent_terminal (original core.rs:23929 onward). The deleted fixtures made a real old agent and tab, removed the agent pane, established that the tab alone kept its tmux session alive, and then checked authoritative listing, NothingAlive refusal, AgentEnded/Unconditional allowance, the terminal-less entry case, and Stop closing the actual surviving tab. These are distinct from a merely stopped agent whose final-screen terminal remains.
The surrounding interface makes this boundary material: tmux.rs:4859–4947 conditionally omits the separate marker query, and :4953–4972 defines the unconditional-marker variant specifically for a surviving lone tab. still_alive_for_delete and tmux_tabs_for_stop must choose the authoritative inventory, including without an agent terminal. Current core.rs:13964–14095 and :14214–14239 do choose it correctly; that is source refutation of an actual destructive bug, not replacement test evidence. In tmux.rs tests, searches for pane_states_with_markers/pane_states calls find no corresponding successful lone-tab guard/Stop fixture. control-codec/pure tab-selection tests can check decoded fixed inputs but not this caller/query/terminal-loss interaction.
Meaningful retained general coverage was checked: e2e/session_lifecycle.rs:3646 onward stops a host agent, then opens a host tab and verifies NothingAlive refusal and later deletion; :3710 onward verifies AgentEnded allows closing tabs. core/tests/host_terminals.rs:333–381 makes a terminal-less entry with a host tab that becomes unreadable and checks uncertainty refusal. These protect the generic consent contract but cannot catch the old tmux marker-query selection regression. terminals.rs:3897–3946 does meaningfully cover forged-marker exclusion from a recorded agent window; ticker.rs:3889 onward also retains an automatic-reap case. Thus the strongest remaining c2 coverage issue is the deleted lone-tab inventory/lifecycle boundary; no separate new forged-marker finding is asserted.
At reviewed revision SPEC_impl.md:2954–2981 expressly still adopts/serves old terminals and SPEC.md:2063–2067 forbids deleting live work beyond the confirmation. Later dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4 ends old terminals at startup and 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333 removes the driver; pinned tip SPEC_impl.md:1888–1909 says every served terminal is a host and old terminals are ended at startup. Therefore this particular legacy discovery oracle is obsolete at tip, but was not obsolete at the reviewed intermediate commit; review charter includes such intermediate changes. The replacement should have kept a driver-built/adopted old-session fixture until old terminals stopped being served, or recorded this as an explicit transitional test coverage loss.
Suggested bucket: other (regression coverage). Confidence: confirmed source comparison only; no runtime test or reproduction. proposed_drop: false; previous proposed drop based only on retained correct guards is superseded. possible_cover: g107/c4, which the parent reports separately considers this exact deleted lone-tab guard test; coordinate/deduplicate with that record, do not silently dismiss the concern. Could-be-highest: preserve the original possible consequences of an unconfirmed Delete killing a live tab and Stop falsely leaving its work alive; no shipped failure route has been established here, so the finding remains test quality rather than actual security/loss of work. Caveats: this is an intermediate-only legacy-test gap; no broad absence of host-tab consent coverage is claimed. Pure forged-marker coverage remains and was actually read. Parent has accepted no drop; keep the strongest original concern for independent adjudication.

# failed-spec test observes the retired terminal kind

Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513

## TLDR
The test intended to prevent launching an agent when its launch instructions cannot be saved now also passes on a failed attempt to start the terminal. The migration leaves its main safety assertion watching tmux, although Farhelm now creates terminal hosts. This weakens regression coverage; it is not evidence that the production ordering is currently wrong.

## Details
The assigned patch's hunk at old core.rs:31075/new :28538 updates the preparation helper's name but leaves create_session_never_launches_tmux_after_a_failed_spec_publish (:28545–28631) using new_with_exe(dummy_exe()) with default seams. It freezes launch/ at mode 0500, submits a create, accepts any ControlMsg::Error, asserts empty in-memory and durable session state, and asserts sup.tmux.pane_states() is empty. New creates exclusively take spawn_agent_in_host (:11749–11797), so no tmux pane can be created regardless of whether a host start was incorrectly attempted. Moreover host_launch.rs:371–378 deliberately selects /nonexistent/farhelm-unit-tests-have-no-host-program for a unit test without host_program. A misplaced/bypassed spec-write guard can therefore reach a host-start attempt and fail for the missing executable; the definitive no-host failure follows the FailedStart::Terminal cleanup (:11873–11946), which can produce the same Error and empty rows/maps that this test accepts. It never asserts the EACCES/spec-publication diagnostic or observes a host start attempt.
The source's current prepare_launch call still precedes start_host (host_launch.rs:454–468, :537–544); this finding concerns the test's ability to protect that boundary after the default-terminal migration. Use an observable host-program seam that would record/allow an attempted start and assert it was never invoked, and require the spec-write failure as the actual refusal. Keep the filesystem-permission fixture if desired. The adjacent converted provenance-ordering test (:26428–26676) and confirmed-absent cleanup test (:31451 onward) witness successful spec publication, not the negative EACCES/no-start boundary.
Contract: the test's own docstring (:28534–28543) promises a real EACCES and no chance for the launch shim to observe a partial spec; the supplied test-authoring checklist requires an observable distinguishing the competing mechanisms and says a shared error alone does not establish cause. SPEC_impl.md:2045–2055 and :2322–2341 describes the host preparation/start boundary. Suggested bucket: other (test quality; no current user-facing failure demonstrated). Confidence: confirmed by source and control-flow analysis only; no execution or reproduction. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none known; no queue/coverage metadata searched. Could-be-highest: no established highest route; a hypothetical ordering regression could affect launched work, but the established consequence here is weakened regression detection, and production ordering is presently correct. Caveat: other tests can catch some related mutations, especially wholly missing spec writes, so this is specifically the failed-publication/no-start assertion becoming ineffective, not a claim that the entire launch pipeline is untested.

## TLDR
The test intended to prove that a failed launch-instruction write prevents any terminal start accepts an error from an attempted terminal start too. Later changes fix its terminal fixture and rename its assertion, but the negative oracle still observes only final cleanup state. This is a regression-test weakness, not an established production ordering error.

## Details
At the reviewed revision, core.rs:28545–28631 uses new_with_exe(dummy_exe()) with default seams, freezes launch/ to 0500 and accepts any ControlMsg::Error plus empty map/store/tmux. host_launch.rs:371–378 selects the deliberately nonexistent unit-test host program; an attempted start can therefore fail for ENOENT, and definitive FailedStart::Terminal cleanup (:11873–11946) can yield the same empty state. Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513

## TLDR
The migration removes a test proving that an uncertain failed create remains visible and keeps its retry unresolved. The retained host equivalent proves only that a database row survives. It could pass if the session disappeared from the running supervisor or its retry were wrongly finalized. Correct current production code does not replace those removed regression oracles.

## Details
Assigned patch lines 980–1103 remove an_ambiguous_tmux_failure_keeps_the_launching_record (old core.rs:33988 onward). Besides retaining one Launching row, that test explicitly asserted sessions.contains_key(row.id), ReservationOutcome::Pending for its key, and ordinary_create_was_refused == false. Those checked three distinct consequences: durable ownership, immediate reachability of Stop/Delete/listing, and a retry that still reconciles instead of replaying a final refusal.
The actual host replacement is e2e/host_creates.rs:1254–1299, an_unusable_host_that_cannot_be_ended_keeps_the_launching_record. Its never-answering listener has a command line the verified signal rejects, so it meaningfully reaches failed cleanup. It asserts the 'may still be running at'/'launching record' diagnostic, one durable host Launching row, and that the listener remains alive. But it calls client.create_session, whose client.rs:3214–3224 explicitly passes None as intent key; it neither lists/resolves the retained session from the running supervisor nor checks a reservation. A wrong Failed settlement for keyed uncertain failure would be invisible, and a missing publish_retained_launch would not change this test's inspected database row or listener. The separate keyed interruption test (host_creates.rs:886–973) deliberately exits via a DuringLaunch simulated crash, before the FailedStart::Terminal cleanup branch, and asserts Created only after a successful retry; it does not cover failed-cleanup publication/settlement. Targeted searches of host tests for the uncertain diagnostic/HostLeft::MayRemain/HostSpawnFailure::Host found no second uncertain-create fixture that supplies these missing assertions.
At tip 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db the same retained host test is :1169–1213 and remains unkeyed with only durable-row/listener checks. The retired tmux symlink-loop/new-session mechanism need not return; extend the existing host fixture with a key and assert its retained session is listed/reachable, reservation remains Pending, and ordinary-create refusal classification does not finalize it.
Contract: SPEC.md:1371–1377 requires one intended create and retained retry identity; SPEC_impl.md:2335–2342 retains uncertain hosts through launching records. Production core.rs:11803–11818 and :11936–11961 correctly keeps the row and publishes it without Failed settlement; no actual orphaned process or incorrect final settlement is established. Suggested bucket: other (lost regression coverage). Confidence: confirmed source analysis; no execution/reproduction. proposed_drop: false; earlier proposed drop based on current correct production code is superseded. possible_cover: none known; parent-supplied g103/f1 concerns unmarked-shell cleanup, a different behavior. Could-be-highest: preserve the original concern that discarding the visible/cleanup handle or finalizing an uncertain intent can hide/orphan running user work, but no such current production route is established, so this finding's established impact remains test quality. Caveat: host path coverage was already narrower in these assertions before this deletion; the regression here is removing the only inspected cross-terminal test oracle instead of carrying its required behavior into the retained host fixture.

Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513

## TLDR
The converted provenance test tells maintainers that cancelling its held start leaves the fake program alive until a release file or its iteration cap ends it. The host-start path now owns a kill-on-drop child and a bounded start timeout. This misstates the fixture's cancellation/cleanup contract; no runtime test failure or leaked process is established.

## Details
The assigned patch converts the fake tmux start into a fake terminal-host first stage and rewrites ReleaseHeldStart's explanation around spawn_agent_in_host. At core.rs:26335–26345 it still says the iteration cap is the fallback when the release cannot land/be acknowledged, and 'so a cancelled hold ends at the cap'; the Drop docstring at :26363–26373 likewise says the cap is what ends the shell on cancellation. The guard itself indeed only writes the release file, but the test's process owner does more than that.
The actual test directly joins spawn_agent_in_host with its observer (core.rs:26534 onward), with no detached task retaining the start future. spawn_agent_in_host directly awaits starting.finish() at core/host_launch.rs:573–575. hosts/spawn.rs:347–360 creates the first-stage Child with kill_on_drop(true); StartingHost holds that Child (:292–300), and finish moves it into a local first (:403–414), then directly awaits its wait under timeout (:419–451). Dropping the test's joined future therefore drops that Child and requests its kill. A start deadline likewise explicitly calls first.start_kill and reaps (:461 onward). The shell cap is still a conservative additional bound, and the release/ack protocol still supports the passing and caught-panic observation ordering; it is not the whole-start cancellation owner described by the changed comment. A kill request is not synchronous proof of process exit, so this finding does not claim the fake is always already reaped when Drop returns.
Attribution: the patch changes the ordering test from its explicit old sup.spawn_agent/fake-tmux future to sup.spawn_agent_in_host/fake-host, not merely a default terminal switch. The removed introductory explanation itself described the old run_bytes/Command::output path without kill_on_drop, explaining why that old fake needed an independent release/cap. Its new replacement drops that qualifier but carries the old cap-only cancellation conclusion into a path with different ownership. This is introduced inaccurate lifecycle prose, not an independent defect sought in retired tmux code.
Later check: at pinned tip 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db core.rs:24247–24256 and :24273–24281 retain the same cancellation/cap assertions, and the host spawn's kill-on-drop ownership remains. Correct the prose to distinguish the release guard's file protocol, the joined host-start future's kill-on-drop/deadline ownership, and the shell's final self-bound. Retain the ack protocol's known observation-ordering rationale rather than removing it on the basis of this documentation finding.
Contract: root documentation rules require accurate lifecycle dependencies and test-harness assumptions, and the supplied checklist requires clear owned-process lifetimes. The source's own StartingHost contract (:280–291) explicitly says dropping it kills the first stage. Suggested bucket: other (documentation correctness). Confidence: confirmed source ownership and prose comparison; no execution/reproduction. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none among supplied neighbour records; g114/g115 concern a different runtime fixture and owner-exit oracle. Could-be-highest: no established or suspected security/loss-of-work route. Caveats: this does not refute c1's meaningful provenance observation boundary and does not add another failed-spec oracle finding; it only corrects the changed guard documentation's process-lifetime model. Cancellation is defense in depth here and is not directly exercised by this test, as the comment itself states. No missing source premise remains for this bounded documentation finding.
